To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
preexposure prophylaix (PrEP) is effective and safe in Africa and can be delivered through a range of service delivery platforms, with high adherence and retention.

PrEP is an effective prevention tool for persons at high risk for acquiring HIV infection and that PrEP programs should be designed to deliver it in combination with other interventions that address risk behaviors and structural drivers of HIV vulnerability.

(1) PrEP has a public health impact in preventing HIV infection; (2) PrEP delivery has to be integrated with HIV testing, counseling and care services, including other biomedical and behavioral prevention strategies, and (3) PrEP delivery should address social drivers of HIV transmission and vulnerability.
